title: Oracle E-Business Suite reflects a script payload (XSS)
summary: An Oracle E-Business Suite page echoes a query parameter into the HTML without encoding it, so a crafted link runs script in the visitor's session. That can steal the session or act as the user. The check sends a harmless marker and confirms it comes back unencoded.

confirm.control: A path that cannot exist, so the site's not found answer is known and a page that reflects the marker is told apart from a soft 404.
confirm.differential: status == 200 and "text/html" in header("content-type") and body_contains("<svg/onload=alert(2)>") and body_differs(control)

reproduce: curl -sk 'https://host/OA_HTML/jtfLOVInProcess.jsp?AAA=AAAAAAAAAA%27%22%3E%3Csvg/onload=alert(2)%3E' and check the body echoes back <svg/onload=alert(2)> unencoded in an HTML response. Also try oksAutoRenewalHelp.jsp?thanks= and ieuiMeetingErrorDisplay.jsp?ErrCode= with the same marker. Unencoded reflection means the parameter is a cross site scripting sink.
remediate: Patch Oracle E-Business Suite to a release that encodes these parameters, and block the affected OA_HTML pages with the Allowed Resources (URL Firewall) framework if they are not needed. Output encode any reflected value.
